content: The Mark I NAAK, also known as the Mark I Kit, is the official United States military designation for the Nerve Agent Antidote Kit. This kit consists of a dual-chamber auto-injector containing two injectable medications: atropine sulfate and pralidoxime chloride. These drugs are specifically designed to counteract the effects of nerve agents. To use the kit, the individual places each injector against their thigh and presses a button. This action activates a spring-loaded needle that is capable of penetrating clothing to deliver the medication. Service members operating in environments where chemical weapons are considered a potential threat are issued three Mark I Kits. Additionally, they are provided with one CANA (Convulsive Antidote, Nerve Agent), which contains diazepam (commonly known as Valium), an anticonvulsant medication. The Mark I Kits and CANA are intended for use in either buddy aid or self-aid scenarios, allowing for the administration of these drugs before decontamination and prior to transferring the patient to definitive medical care. A newer model, the ATNAA (Antidote Treatment Nerve Agent Auto-Injector), combines both atropine and pralidoxime into a single syringe, streamlining the administration process.
